title: Bowel resection (colectomy)
what: The surgeon removes the diseased part of the bowel and joins the ends. Sometimes the bowel is brought out to the belly for a while, as a stoma.
why: For a bowel tumor, severe inflammation, diverticular disease, or a blockage.
duration: surgery usually takes 2 to 4 hours, with 4 to 10 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
How long your bowel habits have changed, and if you have lost weight
Questions about a stoma. Best to discuss them in advance

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Bowel prep
prepare.text: Sometimes a bowel prep or special drink is prescribed the day before. Follow the clinic's plan.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Stoma
prepare.text: If a stoma is possible, a nurse will mark a good spot on your belly in advance and explain the care.

bring: Things for a week in hospital
steps: You change, an IV line is placed, and stockings are put on to prevent clots
The surgeon works through small openings or a cut in the belly
The diseased part of the bowel is removed
The bowel ends are joined, or a stoma is made
The wound is stitched. Sometimes a drain is placed
feel: Belly pain. You will get painkillers
Bloating and weakness in the first days
Stools may be frequent or irregular at first
after: You usually get up and walk on the first day. It speeds recovery
Drinking and eating start gradually, as your doctor allows
No heavy lifting for a few weeks
The lab results will show if further treatment is needed
red_flags: Severe belly pain, a fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or a fast pulse
Vomiting, a swollen belly, or no gas passing
Blood in your stool or black stools
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: It is often temporary and closed after a few months. Sometimes it is permanent. Discuss it with your surgeon.

faq.q: How will my bowel habits change?
faq.a: At first, stools may be frequent. They usually settle over time.

reminders.text: Bowel surgery tomorrow. Do the prep and drinks as the clinic planned. Eat and drink only until the time you were given.
